iti89:1.1: This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant, so I have heard:
iti89:2.1: “Monks, conquered by three forms of false Dhamma–his mind overwhelmed–Devadatta is incurably doomed to deprivation, to hell, for an eon.
iti89:2.3: Conquered by evil desires–his mind overwhelmed–Devadatta is incurably doomed to deprivation, to hell, for the duration of an eon.
iti89:2.4: Conquered by friendship with evil people–his mind overwhelmed–Devadatta is incurably doomed to deprivation, to hell, for the duration of an eon.
iti89:2.5: And, there being something further to be done, he nevertheless stopped halfway with a lower modicum of distinctive attainment.
iti89:2.6: Conquered by these three forms of false Dhamma–his mind overwhelmed–Devadatta is incurably doomed to deprivation, to hell, for an eon.”
iti89:3.1:
May no one in the world
ever
iti89:3.3:
Know that
through that
evil desire,
iti89:3.4:
his destination’s that
of all who have evil desires.
iti89:4.1:
I’ve heard how Devadatta,
–regarded as wise, composed,
incandescent with honor–
iti89:5.3:
and fell to the four-gated, fearful place:
Avīci, unmitigated hell.
iti89:6.1:
Whoever plots against
one free of corruption
iti89:7.1:
Whoever might think
of polluting the ocean
with a pot of poison,
iti89:7.4: for the mass of water is great.
iti89:8.1:
So it is
when anyone attacks with abuse
the Tathāgata
iti89:8.4: for abuse doesn’t grow on him.
iti89:9.1:
A wise person should make friends,
should associate,
with a person like him–
iti89:9.3: whose path a monk can pursue
iti89:9.4:
and reach the ending
of suffering & stress.
